transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I get stuck doing the same checks and routines over and over until I can’t finish anything, even when I know it makes no sense. It's gotten to the point where it's completely taking over my day, and I just don't know how to stop it.
Do these repetitive actions and routines start because of unwanted, distressing thoughts, worries, or mental images that keep popping into your mind?

Yes, that's exactly what happens. I get these vivid pictures in my head of a house I worked on catching fire or a deck collapsing because of some tiny mistake I might have made. To try and quiet those thoughts, I feel forced to check things like the stove, the locks, or my tools over and over again so nothing terrible happens.
How long have you been experiencing these distressing thoughts and checking routines, and roughly how much time do they take up in your daily life?

These issues have been building up and getting worse over the past few years, especially as I took on more responsibility at work. Now, a single checking routine can easily take an hour or more, and it eats up so much of my day that I can't finish basic tasks, get dinner ready, or even leave the house on time.
Do you feel these thoughts and images are coming from your own mind, and do you ever try to resist the urge to do these checks?

Yes, I know they're coming from my own mind, even though they feel incredibly intrusive. I do try to resist them by telling myself everything is fine and that the jobs passed inspection years ago, but the anxiety just builds up until I have to give in and check.

latest_inference.note: The patient exhibits both clear obsessions (intrusive, distressing thoughts and images of fires or collapses) and compulsions (repetitive checking routines of stoves, locks, and tools). These symptoms have been present for years, take up significant time, are recognized as originating from the patient's own mind, and are resisted unsuccessfully. This satisfies the ICD-10 criteria for F42.2 (Mixed obsessive thoughts and acts). No further information is needed to confirm this diagnosis.

These symptoms originate from his own mind, are resisted with difficulty, and cause significant distress and functional impairment, taking up more than an hour a day. This clinical picture of mixed obsessions and compulsions meets the ICD-10 criteria for F42.2 (Mixed obsessional thoughts and acts).
